chapter: Producing, state of New Orleans music
title: New Orleans exposure, disco and Chocolate Milk
summary: He responds on what New Orleans deserves, disco and the band Chocolate Milk.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: It can be a downfall, but as far as what we deserve, has always been a very sticky subject to me. What do we deserve? Any man deserves. Yeah. Who are we? And just how much are we contributing to what we deserve? Which are... And I'm surely not knocking for what we've contributed. It's just that it's a constant flow. It's not something that just happened a long time ago, and you're still waiting for your just do's. You stay in the running. You stay in the race. What do you think of disco? I think it's very much today. I'm for what's today. If I didn't like disco, I would do a little more homework or investigation, and I would even try to. Being because this is what we're doing. And I like music, and this is more music. That's what I think of it. Now, whether I just like disco, yes. I like disco. I don't dance. I would feel terribly overexposed. But I do like the concept of disco, and I like the artistic release that disco allows people to have. I mean, it can really be theatrical on a dance floor nowadays,

and don't feel overdone. Do you have trouble with it? It doesn't seem like to have that much emotion. Well, I mean, it's like fun music, but it's not. Some of disco seems like it's devoid of emotions. Dr. John doesn't seem to like it at all. He said it's just had no human feeling in it. I think it's just going too far.
I understand. I can understand. It's a matter of opinion.
Are there any local artists, up-and-coming artists, that you think our listening audience ought to be keeping their ears glued for?

Local folk? Yeah. Chocolate milk, of course. I do believe in chocolate milk very strongly, and never because of what was yesterday, and I do mean the real yesterday, or today, but so much because of how they run their operation, the feeling they have for each other. All of these things are going to come out in music, and the music that they're making. They're very choicy about it. Whether it sells or not right now, it is important, but it's in all good directions, and I expect the results of good things to be good, so yes.
